newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Germany unsatisfied with French EMU moves -- Welteke.
newsitem.headline: Germany unsatisfied with French EMU moves -- Welteke.

text.p: Germany is not satisfied with the moves made by France so far to meet convergence criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU), Ernst Welteke, a member of the Bundesbank council, said on Friday.
"No, we are not satisfied and we are not pleased," Welteke told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview in Singapore.

But he added that Germany is having its own difficulties. "We have to look to our own problems in Germany. If a forecast for 3.5 deficit is right, this is a half percent above the Maastricht criteria and this is not very good."
Some economists are predicting that Germany's deficit-to-GDP ratio may be 3.5 percent in 1997.
"We are not alone on the earth, we should not blame the others," he added.
Despite these problems, Welteke said he believes that EMU will still go ahead as planned, but criticised window-dressing moves that some countries might use to meet EMU criteria.

"The new currency needs confidence. And if they do some tricks in the upcoming member states, it's not very good for the public. The public will not have enough confidence in the stability of the new currency," he said.
He said this would require debate with Germany's colleagues in other prospective EMU member countries, but that they would rely on statistics to prove the stability of the new currency.
